# `guide_pulse`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Issue a manual guide pulse in one direction for a duration in milliseconds.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (native handler, 64-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x7f0d0 (64-bit build) |

Parses direction (string, case-insensitive compass or up/down/left/right names) and amount (integer milliseconds) and performs a native manual Move on the mount or the optional AO device. It refuses while calibrating or guiding. A success reply (result 0) is returned after the Move call; whether the move has physically finished depends on the selected device subtype. Completion and guide events are unresolved.

Side effects: Sends a manual guide pulse to the mount or AO device through the virtual Move call; no duration range check.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"guide_pulse"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | no | - | Either a named object or a positional array [direction, amount, which]. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | amount missing or not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 105 | direction missing or not a string (two string-type check sites exist; the second, possibly the which selector, is unresolved) | `expected string param` |
| 318 | Target guide device not connected | `device not connected` |
| 319 | Guider is calibrating or guiding | `cannot issue guide pulse while calibrating or guiding` |
| 320 | The native Move call fails | `move failed` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

## Example

Request, object - Values invented:

```json
{"id":50,"method":"guide_pulse","params":{"direction":"north","amount":500}}
```

Request, positional - Values invented:

```json
{"id":51,"method":"guide_pulse","params":["East",250]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"guide_pulse","result":0,"code":0,"id":50}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"guide_pulse","error":"cannot issue guide pulse while calibrating or guiding","code":319,"id":52}
```
